coaching.whyItMatters: The Biceps Curl builds strength and size in your biceps. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
instructions: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.
Set a tall torso with your upper arms pinned against your sides.
Start with your arms straight and the load under control.
Bend your elbows and curl the load up while keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze at the top for a beat.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides throughout.
Keep the tension on your biceps and stop your elbows from drifting forward.
Turn your pinky slightly up at the top to finish the squeeze.
Lower all the way until your arm is straight each rep.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start the load moving.
Letting the elbows drift forward to lift the load higher.
Cutting the lower-half of the range short.
advancedNotes: Slow the lowering phase to three counts to add time under tension.

progressionGuidance.regressionReason: Drop back to Machine Biceps Curl to groove the movement before you add load or complexity.

coachingExtended.equipmentSetup: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Swinging the torso to start the load moving.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A torso swing starts the curl with momentum instead of your biceps.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stand tall and keep your upper arms fixed against your sides.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the elbows drift forward to lift the load higher.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Moving the elbows turns a curl into a partial front raise and takes tension off your biceps.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your elbows under your shoulders and stop the curl where your upper arm wants to move.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the lower-half of the range short.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the bottom half leaves strength and size on the table.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Straighten your arm fully at the bottom of each rep.

beginnerNotes: Pick a load you can lift without swinging your body.
coachingExtended.breathingGuidance: Exhale as you curl up, breathe in as you lower.
coachingExtended.tempoGuidance: Curl with control and lower for about two counts.
coachingExtended.rangeOfMotionNotes: Move from a fully straight arm to a hard squeeze at the top. Take the biceps through its full working range each rep.
coachingExtended.difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you balance and control the weight yourself, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.
coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Biceps Curl is an isolation barbell movement. You balance and drive the bar yourself, so groove the bar path before chasing weight. Your working limb moves freely, so keep the joint you are training under control. Add load gradually as your control improves.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Box Squat builds strength and size in your quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.
Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Take a full breath into your belly and brace before you descend.
Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
tips: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward under load.
Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.
safetyNotes: Reduce the load if you lose control of the movement.
Stop the set if you feel sharp pain.
advancedNotes: Add a pause in the bottom position to build strength out of the hole.

progressionGuidance.progressionReason: Move up to Barbell Back Squat once you can control this one for all your reps.

coachingExtended.equipmentSetup: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the knees cave inward under load.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Caved knees are a weaker position and rob power from the lift.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Push your knees out toward your little toes as you descend and stand.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Hips shooting up first tips you forward and turns the squat into a good morning.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lead with your chest and drive your hips and shoulders up at the same rate.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the depth short above parallel.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

beginnerNotes: Start with a box or bench behind you to learn consistent depth.
coachingExtended.breathingGuidance: Take a big breath at the top, hold it through the descent and drive, then exhale at the top.
coachingExtended.tempoGuidance: Lower under control for about two counts, then stand with intent.
coachingExtended.rangeOfMotionNotes: Aim for thighs at or below parallel while keeping your heels flat on the floor. Take the quadriceps through its full working range each rep.
coachingExtended.spottingNotes: Use a spotter or set safety pins when the load is heavy on this squat, so you can bail a failed rep safely.
coachingExtended.difficultyExplanation: Rated Beginner because you balance and control the weight yourself, and it coordinates several joints at once.
coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Box Squat is a compound barbell movement. You balance and drive the bar yourself, so groove the bar path before chasing weight. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Calf Raise builds strength and size in your calves. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
instructions: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.
Set the balls of your feet on a stable surface with your heels free to drop.
Find a light hold for balance if you need it.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause for a beat at the top.
Lower under control until you feel a full stretch through your calves.
tips: Rise as high onto your toes as possible at the top.
Rise all the way onto your toes and squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower under control into a full stretch at the bottom.
Pause briefly at the top to remove any bounce.
commonMistakes: Bouncing through short, fast reps.
Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
Letting the ankles roll outward as you rise.
advancedNotes: Add a two-count pause in the stretched position for extra range.

progressionGuidance.regressionReason: Drop back to Seated Calf Raise Machine to groove the movement before you add load or complexity.

coachingExtended.equipmentSetup: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Bouncing through short, fast reps.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Short bounces use the tendon’s spring instead of your calves, so they do less work.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Pause at the top and control a full stretch at the bottom.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the stretch short at the bottom.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the stretch removes the part of the range that builds the most.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Let your heels drop below the platform for a full stretch.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the ankles roll outward as you rise.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Rolling out sends force through the outside of your foot instead of your calves.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Drive evenly through your big toe and keep your ankles stacked.

beginnerNotes: Do the movement on flat ground before adding a deficit or load.
coachingExtended.breathingGuidance: Exhale as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
coachingExtended.tempoGuidance: Rise with control, pause at the top, then lower slowly.
coachingExtended.rangeOfMotionNotes: Move from a deep heel-dropped stretch to a full rise on your toes. Take the calves through its full working range each rep.
coachingExtended.difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you balance and control the weight yourself, and it works one joint, so it is simpler to learn.
coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Calf Raise is an isolation barbell movement. You balance and drive the bar yourself, so groove the bar path before chasing weight. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. Add load gradually as your control improves.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Front Rack Carry builds strength and size in your forearms, trapezius and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.
Pick up the load with a flat back and stand tall.
Set your shoulders back and down before you start walking.
Walk with short, deliberate steps while staying tall.
Keep the load from swinging by holding your sides tight.
Set the load down under control at the end of the distance rather than dropping it.
tips: Stand tall and walk with short, controlled steps.
Keep a firm grip and let your forearms do the work.
Keep the load steady rather than letting it swing.
Keep your shoulders back and down for the full distance.
commonMistakes: Leaning to one side under an uneven load.
Taking long, rushed strides that let the load sway.
Rounding the shoulders forward under the load.
advancedNotes: Increase the distance or load while keeping your torso perfectly upright.

coachingExtended.equipmentSetup: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Leaning to one side under an uneven load.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Leaning lets the load win and takes the anti-lean work off your trunk.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stay stacked and tall, resisting the pull to one side.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Taking long, rushed strides that let the load sway.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A swaying load pulls you around and takes the anti-sway work off your trunk.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Shorten your steps and keep a steady, controlled pace.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rounding the shoulders forward under the load.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Rounded shoulders are a weaker position to carry and hold the load.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your chest up and your shoulders pulled back for the full distance.

beginnerNotes: Start with a shorter distance and a load you can control the whole way.
coachingExtended.breathingGuidance: Breathe steadily and rhythmically throughout the carry.
coachingExtended.tempoGuidance: Move at a controlled, deliberate walking pace.
coachingExtended.rangeOfMotionNotes: Cover the target distance or time while holding position. Take the forearms and trapezius through their full working range each rep.
coachingExtended.difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you balance and control the weight yourself.
coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Front Rack Carry is a barbell movement. You balance and drive the bar yourself, so groove the bar path before chasing weight. Add load gradually as your control improves.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Glute Bridge builds strength and size in your glutes, adductors, erector spinae and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.
Set your upper back or shoulders as the pivot and your feet flat, about hip-width and close to your hips.
Tuck your ribs down and brace before the first rep.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top for a beat.
Lower your hips under control back toward the floor.
tips: Drive through your heels, not your toes.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.
Finish each rep by squeezing your glutes at the top, not by arching your lower back.
Keep your ribs down and your chin slightly tucked so the work stays in your glutes.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to push the hips higher.
Pushing through the toes so the heels lift.
Rushing reps without a real glute squeeze at the top.
safetyNotes: Reduce the load if you lose control of the movement.
Stop the set if you feel sharp pain.
advancedNotes: Add a pause at the top or increase the resistance once you own the movement.

progressionGuidance.progressionReason: Move up to Barbell Deadlift once you can control this one for all your reps.

coachingExtended.equipmentSetup: Load the bar evenly on both sides and secure it with collars before you lift.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Arching the lower back to push the hips higher.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Extra height from your spine, not your hips, means your glutes do less of the work.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stop at a straight line from shoulders to knees and squeeze your glutes.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Pushing through the toes so the heels lift.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: On your toes your glutes do less and the hip drive weakens.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your whole foot down and drive through your heels.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing reps without a real glute squeeze at the top.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the squeeze leaves the strongest part of the contraction untrained.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Pause and squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.

beginnerNotes: Start with bodyweight and learn to feel your glutes doing the work before adding resistance.

coachingExtended.tempoGuidance: Drive up with intent and lower under control for about two counts.
coachingExtended.rangeOfMotionNotes: Lift until your hips reach a straight shoulder-to-knee line, then lower under control. Take the glutes through its full working range each rep.
coachingExtended.difficultyExplanation: Rated Beginner because you balance and control the weight yourself, and it coordinates several joints at once.
coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Glute Bridge is a compound barbell movement. You balance and drive the bar yourself, so groove the bar path before chasing weight. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Deep Squat Hold builds strength and size in your quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Set a tall chest and brace before you descend.
Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
tips: Keep your weight balanced over the middle of your foot.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Keep your chest up as you descend and stand.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward.
Letting the heels lift off the floor.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.
advancedNotes: Slow the descent or add a pause at the bottom to increase the challenge.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the knees cave inward.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Knees caving in is a weaker position and takes force off your glutes.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Push your knees out toward your little toes as you descend and stand.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the heels lift off the floor.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: On your toes you lose your base and shift the squat onto your knees.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your whole foot planted and your weight over the mid-foot.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the depth short above parallel.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

beginnerNotes: Lower to a box or bench behind you to learn consistent depth.
coachingExtended.breathingGuidance: Breathe in on the way down, exhale as you stand.
coachingExtended.tempoGuidance: Lower under control for about two counts, then stand with intent.
coachingExtended.rangeOfMotionNotes: Lower to at least thighs-parallel and stand up tall each rep. Take the quadriceps through its full working range each rep.
coachingExtended.difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you manage only your own bodyweight, and it coordinates several joints at once.
coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Deep Squat Hold is a compound bodyweight movement. You move and stabilise your own bodyweight, so change leverage to progress rather than adding weight. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. Add load gradually as your control improves.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Glute Bridge Iso Hold builds strength and size in your glutes, adductors, erector spinae and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Set your upper back or shoulders as the pivot and your feet flat, about hip-width and close to your hips.
Tuck your ribs down and brace before the first rep.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top for a beat.
Lower your hips under control back toward the floor.
tips: Drive through your heels, not your toes.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Finish each rep by squeezing your glutes at the top, not by arching your lower back.
Keep your ribs down and your chin slightly tucked so the work stays in your glutes.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to push the hips higher.
Pushing through the toes so the heels lift.
Rushing reps without a real glute squeeze at the top.
advancedNotes: Add a pause at the top or increase the resistance once you own the movement.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Arching the lower back to push the hips higher.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Extra height from your spine, not your hips, means your glutes do less of the work.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stop at a straight line from shoulders to knees and squeeze your glutes.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Pushing through the toes so the heels lift.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: On your toes your glutes do less and the hip drive weakens.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your whole foot down and drive through your heels.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing reps without a real glute squeeze at the top.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the squeeze leaves the strongest part of the contraction untrained.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Pause and squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.

beginnerNotes: Start with bodyweight and learn to feel your glutes doing the work before adding resistance.
coachingExtended.breathingGuidance: Exhale as you drive your hips up, breathe in as you lower.
coachingExtended.tempoGuidance: Drive up with intent and lower under control for about two counts.
coachingExtended.rangeOfMotionNotes: Lift until your hips reach a straight shoulder-to-knee line, then lower under control. Take the glutes through its full working range each rep.
coachingExtended.difficultyExplanation: Rated Beginner because you manage only your own bodyweight, and it coordinates several joints at once.
coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Glute Bridge Iso Hold is a compound bodyweight movement. You move and stabilise your own bodyweight, so change leverage to progress rather than adding weight. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. It suits newer athletes and is a good place to build the pattern.

coaching.whyItMatters: The McGill Curl-Up builds strength and size in your rectus abdominis and obliques. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Set your position and take the slack out of your midsection before you begin.
Start each rep from a controlled, stable position.
Move slowly and deliberately through the working range.
Pause briefly where your midsection is working hardest.
Control the return rather than dropping quickly at the end.
tips: Move under control — no yanking or rushing the reps.
Curl your ribs toward your hips and feel your abs shorten.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Curl your ribs toward your hips rather than pulling with your neck.
Keep the tension on your midsection, not your hip flexors or lower back.
commonMistakes: Pulling on the neck or head to complete the rep.
Rushing through reps with momentum.
Arching the lower back away from a braced position.
advancedNotes: Add a pause at the hardest point of the range for extra tension.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Pulling on the neck or head to complete the rep.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Pulling your head does the work your abs should, so your midsection gets less out of it.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your hands light and lead the movement from your midsection.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rushing through reps with momentum.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Momentum does the work your abs should, so the set does less.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Slow each rep down and control both directions.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Arching the lower back away from a braced position.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A loose lower back leaks force and takes the work off your abs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your ribs down and your midsection tight through the whole rep.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Scapular Push-Up builds strength and size in your chest, front deltoids and triceps. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Set your hands about shoulder-width, slightly wider than your chest.
Set a straight line from your head to your heels and brace before you begin.
Lower your chest under control toward the floor.
Keep your elbows tucked to about 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep a straight line from your head to your heels throughout.
Think about squeezing your chest to drive the movement, not just pushing with your arms.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.
Tuck your elbows to about 45 degrees rather than flaring them wide.
Lower until your chest is just off the floor for a full range.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Only lowering partway before pressing back up.
advancedNotes: Elevate your feet or pause at the bottom to make it harder.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Sagging hips break the plank line and shift load to your lower back.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Squeeze your glutes and keep a straight line from head to heels.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Flared elbows put your shoulders in a weaker, less comfortable pressing position.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Point your elbows back toward your hips as you lower.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Only lowering partway before pressing back up.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Half reps train a fraction of the range and build less.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your chest is just off the floor each rep.

coachingExtended.tempoGuidance: Lower for about two counts, then press up with intent.
coachingExtended.rangeOfMotionNotes: Lower until your chest is just off the floor and press to straight arms. Take the chest through its full working range each rep.
coachingExtended.difficultyExplanation: Rated Intermediate because you manage only your own bodyweight, and it coordinates several joints at once.
coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Scapular Push-Up is a compound bodyweight movement. Add load gradually as your control improves.

Lead with your elbows and raise the load to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower the load under control to the start.
tips: Lead with your elbows and stop at shoulder height.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders and pull your elbows back and apart.
Own the full range of every rep before you add reps or make it harder.

Lower under control rather than dropping the load.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Alternating Curl builds strength and size in your biceps. As an isolation movement, it targets those muscles directly to build size and balance.
instructions: Choose a pair you can control for every planned rep and get them into position cleanly.
Set a tall torso with your upper arms pinned against your sides.
Start with your arms straight and the load under control.
Bend your elbows and curl the load up while keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze at the top for a beat.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides throughout.
Keep the tension on your biceps and stop your elbows from drifting forward.
Control each dumbbell independently so your stronger side doesn’t take over.
Turn your pinky slightly up at the top to finish the squeeze.
Lower all the way until your arm is straight each rep.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start the load moving.
Letting the elbows drift forward to lift the load higher.
Cutting the lower-half of the range short.
advancedNotes: Slow the lowering phase to three counts to add time under tension.

coachingExtended.equipmentSetup: Choose a pair you can control for every planned rep and get them into position cleanly.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Swinging the torso to start the load moving.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A torso swing starts the curl with momentum instead of your biceps.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stand tall and keep your upper arms fixed against your sides.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Letting the elbows drift forward to lift the load higher.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Moving the elbows turns a curl into a partial front raise and takes tension off your biceps.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your elbows under your shoulders and stop the curl where your upper arm wants to move.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the lower-half of the range short.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Skipping the bottom half leaves strength and size on the table.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Straighten your arm fully at the bottom of each rep.

coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Alternating Curl is an isolation dumbbell movement. Each dumbbell is balanced on its own, so both sides have to pull their own weight. coaching.whyItMatters: The Alternating Lunge Jump builds strength and size in your quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Set a box height you can land on comfortably and make sure it is stable and won’t slide.
Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Take a full breath into your belly and brace before you descend.
Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
tips: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward under load.
Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.
advancedNotes: Add a pause in the bottom position to build strength out of the hole.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Forward Hurdle Hop builds strength and size in your glutes, adductors, erector spinae and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Set a box height you can land on comfortably and make sure it is stable and won’t slide.
Set your feet about hip-width with the load close to your shins.
Set your back flat and take a breath into your belly before you pull.
Push your hips back and let your knees bend slightly as the load lowers.
Keep the load brushing your legs the whole way.
Stand up by driving your hips forward until you are tall.
tips: Push your hips back until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.
Keep the load in contact with your legs from start to finish.
Finish by squeezing your glutes, not by leaning back past standing.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as the load leaves the floor.
Turning the hinge into a squat by bending the knees too early.
Hyperextending and leaning back at the top.
advancedNotes: Pause just below the knee to build control in the stretched position.

coachingExtended.equipmentSetup: Set a box height you can land on comfortably and make sure it is stable and won’t slide.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rounding the lower back as the load leaves the floor.

mistakeCorrections.correction: Set your back flat and lift your chest before the load moves.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Turning the hinge into a squat by bending the knees too early.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Early knee bend takes the stretch and work off your hamstrings and glutes.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Send your hips backward first and let the knees follow.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Hyperextending and leaning back at the top.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Leaning back past standing loads your lower back and adds nothing to the lift.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Stop when you are standing tall with your glutes squeezed.

coachingExtended.difficultyConsiderations: The Forward Hurdle Hop is a compound plyometric movement. The box fixes the height, so land and stand on it under full control. Your hands or feet stay planted, so you move your body against the resistance. Add load gradually as your control improves.

Set your feet about shoulder-width with your toes turned out slightly.
Take a full breath into your belly and brace before you descend.
Break at the hips and knees together and lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
Complete all your reps on one side, then repeat with the other, matching the reps on your weaker side.
tips: Keep the load stacked over the middle of your foot.
Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward under load.
Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.
advancedNotes: Add a pause in the bottom position to build strength out of the hole.

progressionGuidance.regressionReason: Drop back to Step-Up Box Jump to groove the movement before you add load or complexity.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: Hips shooting up first tips you forward and turns the squat into a good morning.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lead with your chest and drive your hips and shoulders up at the same rate.

mistakeCorrections.mistake: Cutting the depth short above parallel.
mistakeCorrections.whyItMatters: A shallow squat trains a fraction of the range and much less of your legs.
mistakeCorrections.correction: Lower until your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Anti-Rotation Hold builds strength and size in your rectus abdominis, hip flexors and obliques. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Anchor the band securely, check there is no slack at the start, and expect the tension to rise through the range.
Set your position and take the slack out of your midsection before you begin.
Start each rep from a controlled, stable position.
Move slowly and deliberately through the working range.
Pause briefly where your midsection is working hardest.
Control the return rather than dropping quickly at the end.
tips: Move under control — no yanking or rushing the reps.
Curl your ribs toward your hips and feel your abs shorten.
Match your effort to the band — its resistance climbs toward the end of the range.
Curl your ribs toward your hips rather than pulling with your neck.
Keep the tension on your midsection, not your hip flexors or lower back.
commonMistakes: Pulling on the neck or head to complete the rep.
Rushing through reps with momentum.
Arching the lower back away from a braced position.
Letting the band snap you back through the last part of the range.
advancedNotes: Add a pause at the hardest point of the range for extra tension.

mistakeCorrections.correction: Keep your ribs down and your midsection tight through the whole rep.

Support your weight on the handles or bars with your arms straight and your shoulders pulled down.
Set a slight forward lean and brace before you lower.
Lower under control by bending your elbows until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Keep your elbows tracking back rather than flaring wide.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Lower until your upper arms reach about parallel to the floor.
Think about squeezing your chest to drive the movement, not just pushing with your arms.
Match your effort to the band — its resistance climbs toward the end of the range.
Keep your elbows tracking back over your wrists, not flaring out.

Only dipping a few inches instead of reaching depth.
Letting the elbows flare wide as you press.

instructions: Anchor the band securely, check there is no slack at the start, and expect the tension to rise through the range.
Set a tall torso with your upper arms pinned against your sides.
Start with your arms straight and the load under control.
Bend your elbows and curl the load up while keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze at the top for a beat.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides throughout.
Keep the tension on your biceps and stop your elbows from drifting forward.
Match your effort to the band — its resistance climbs toward the end of the range.
Turn your pinky slightly up at the top to finish the squeeze.
Lower all the way until your arm is straight each rep.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start the load moving.
Letting the elbows drift forward to lift the load higher.
Cutting the lower-half of the range short.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Split Squat builds strength and size in your quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.

Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
Complete all your reps on one side, then repeat with the other, matching the reps on your weaker side.

Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.

Cutting the depth short above parallel.
Letting the band snap you back through the last part of the range.
advancedNotes: Add a pause in the bottom position to build strength out of the hole.

Set the load down under control at the end of the distance rather than dropping it.

coaching.whyItMatters: The Suspension Trainer Squat builds strength and size in your quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings and rectus abdominis. As a compound movement, it trains several muscles together and carries over to real-world strength and power.
instructions: Check the anchor is secure and set the strap length, then load your weight gradually to test it before full reps.

Drive through the middle of your foot to stand back up.
Complete all your reps on one side, then repeat with the other, matching the reps on your weaker side.

Drive through your knees and feel the front of your thighs work.
Set the difficulty with your foot position and how far you lean into the straps.
Let your knees track in line with your toes.
Push your knees out as you descend into the bottom.

Rising hips-first so the load shifts forward onto your toes.
Cutting the depth short above parallel.
advancedNotes: Add a pause in the bottom position to build strength out of the hole.
